description: This PR adds yet another Jetpack library called [App Startup](https://developer.android.com/topic/libraries/app-startup) in order to boost startup time of the application. Here is a comparison chart for better understanding. Looks like there is a significant improvement at startup. If you want to test yourself, execute below command in your terminal: Please only take care of `Total Time` row. `adb shell am start-activity -W -n com.google.samples.apps.iosched/.ui.LauncherActivity`

comments.body: To lazily initialize `Timber` after the app is created. [Lazy initialization](https://developer.android.com/topic/libraries/app-startup#manual) is suggested if possible to reduce startup cost.
These two used to be called before `onCreate` so that I didn't init these lazily as these will be initialized automatically before `onCreate` is called.

```suggestion
    fun analyticsHelperInitializer(): AnalyticsHelperInitializer
```

I understand this works as you expect and is nice to read. However, an entry point's responsibility is not _injecting_ classes, entry points _expose_ instances from the graph.

```suggestion
        analyticsHelperInitializer = InitializerEntryPoint.resolve(context). analyticsHelperInitializer()
```

As commented above, I'd rather not have entry points behave like Dagger components. Also, the `@Inject` from `analyticsHelper` can be removed and can be made `private`.

Thanks!
I think `analyticsHelperInitializer` should be `analyticsHelper` instead, right? Cause we have an instance of `AnalyticsHelper` from the graph.
Sorry, I didn't get this, why `EntryPoint` returns `initializer` instance instead of `dependency` which is `AnalyticsHelper` in this class?
Yes, sorry! I meant to say `analyticsHelper` instead :) thank you!
Yeah, sorry, meant `analyticsHelper = InitializerEntryPoint.resolve(context). analyticsHelper()` instead
